name: Portland

electric.name: Portland General Electric (PGE)
electric.serves: Oregon electric utility; says it 'powers nearly half of Oregon's population'. Efficiency incentives for its Oregon customers come from Energy Trust of Oregon.

electric.name: Pacific Power
electric.serves: 820,000 customers in 243 communities across Oregon, Washington and California; Oregon customers' efficiency incentives come from Energy Trust

gas.name: NW Natural
gas.serves: About two million people across the Pacific Northwest, including Oregon and Southwest Washington; Energy Trust incentives cover NW Natural customers in both states

utilities.notes: Energy Trust of Oregon is not a utility but runs efficiency incentives for Oregon customers of PGE, Pacific Power, NW Natural, Cascade Natural Gas and Avista, and for Southwest Washington customers of NW Natural. In Clark County, WA, electric efficiency programs come from Clark Public Utilities.

auditPrograms.name: Portland Home Energy Score (required at listing)
auditPrograms.runBy: City of Portland Bureau of Planning and Sustainability; helpdesk run by Earth Advantage (hesinfo@earthadvantage.org, 503-278-5347); assessments by independent authorized Home Energy Assessors
auditPrograms.cost: Set by each independent assessor (the City recommends calling more than one to compare cost and scheduling)
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Required for sellers publicly advertising most homes within Portland's jurisdictional boundary (some Clackamas and Washington county addresses are inside it); any homeowner may get one voluntarily
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: About 45 minutes to an hour on site including attic and crawl spaces; 70+ data points modeled into a U.S. DOE Home Energy Score and Report, posted to the Green Building Registry; a score can be reused for up to eight years if nothing assessed has changed
auditPrograms.howToBook: Contact an authorized Home Energy Assessor (list linked from the City's HES for Home Sellers page) before listing

auditPrograms.name: Energy Friendly Homes (PCEF single-family program) - walk-through and energy assessment
auditPrograms.runBy: Funded by the Portland Clean Energy Community Benefits Fund (PCEF); administrator not named on the site
auditPrograms.cost: No-cost or low-cost (site does not say which items are free)
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Homeowners in Portland city limits with household income below 150% of area median income; renter opportunities expected in late 2026
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: Walk-through with an Energy Specialist, then an on-site energy assessment by a contractor to build an upgrade plan (insulation, ducted or ductless heat pumps, heat pump water heaters; up to 30% of project funds can cover related repairs such as radon or asbestos mitigation, roof, electrical, dry rot or pests); typical project takes 4-6 months
auditPrograms.howToBook: Apply online at energyfriendlyhomes.com or call 971-399-7742 (info@EnergyFriendlyHomes.com); the program warns of phishing impersonators
auditPrograms.status: open (online application live; site modified July 30, 2026)

auditPrograms.name: Energy Trust of Oregon online home energy assessment
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Anyone; designed for Energy Trust-served homes
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: A short online questionnaire that returns personalized recommendations (no in-home visit)
auditPrograms.howToBook: Online via the 'Take our home energy assessment' link on Energy Trust's Home Upgrades + Incentives page

auditPrograms.name: Clark Public Utilities free in-home energy review (Clark County, WA)
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Clark Public Utilities customers, including gas-heated homes
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: 60-90 minute visit by an Energy Counselor reviewing usage, systems, insulation levels and duct leakage (no blower door or infrared camera), with advice on upgrades

rebates.name: Energy Trust insulation incentives
rebates.amount: Oregon owner-occupied single-family: attic $1.25/sq ft (existing R-18 or less, insulate to R-38+), wall $1.50/sq ft, floor $0.75/sq ft; Savings Within Reach (income-qualified), rental and attached homes get more (attic $1.50, wall $2.25, floor $1.00/sq ft). SW Washington (NW Natural gas-heated): attic, wall and floor $1.25/sq ft, more for Savings Within Reach
rebates.whoQualifies: Homes primarily heated by fuel from PGE, Pacific Power, NW Natural, Cascade Natural Gas or Avista (Oregon) or NW Natural (SW Washington); some measures may be self-installed

rebates.name: Energy Trust heat pump incentives
rebates.amount: Ducted heat pump replacing an electric forced-air furnace: $1,000 (Oregon owner, single-family/manufactured) or $3,000 (Savings Within Reach, rentals, attached homes); extended-capacity heat pump with no gas backup: $1,000 or $2,000; ductless heat pump replacing electric resistance heat in the main living space: $800 or $1,800
rebates.whoQualifies: Energy Trust-served Oregon homes; equipment and installation requirements on the incentive table

rebates.name: Energy Trust heat pump water heater instant discounts
rebates.amount: $1,200 instant discount when a licensed contractor buys a Tier 3+ unit through a participating distributor (replacing a standard electric water heater); $1,000 instant discount for in-store purchase at participating retailers (limit one)
rebates.whoQualifies: Oregon customers served by PGE, Pacific Power, NW Natural, Cascade Natural Gas or Avista; existing homes only; no post-purchase application

rebates.name: Oregon Heat Pump Purchase Program (HP3)
rebates.runBy: Oregon Department of Energy (EPA Climate Pollution Reduction Grant funds)
rebates.amount: $2,000 per heat pump, taken off the price by an approved contractor
rebates.whoQualifies: Owner-occupied homes, rentals and new construction in Oregon; HSPF2 8.1+ and SEER2 16+
rebates.status: owner-occupied homes: Round 1 and Round 2 funding fully reserved; rental property and new construction funding still available (ODOE accepting reservations and applications)

rebates.name: Community Heat Pump Deployment Program (regional administrators)
rebates.runBy: Oregon Department of Energy via regional administrators (Earth Advantage for the Metro, North Coast and Mid-Valley regions)
rebates.amount: Up to $5,000 (minimum efficiency) or $7,000 (higher efficiency) per heat pump, plus up to $4,000 grant for panel, weatherization or structural repairs
rebates.status: Metro region (Clackamas, Multnomah, Washington counties) and Mid-Valley (incl. Yamhill County): funding fully reserved, not accepting applications; North Coast (incl. Columbia County): funding available, accepting applications

rebates.name: Oregon Rental Home Heat Pump Program
rebates.whoQualifies: Rental dwellings and rented manufactured-home/RV spaces
rebates.status: closed: general program funding completely reserved; not accepting applications (separate tribal allocations still open)

rebates.name: Energy Friendly Homes (PCEF Strategic Program 3)
rebates.runBy: City of Portland, Portland Clean Energy Community Benefits Fund
rebates.amount: No-cost or low-cost upgrades; program budget $140 million over five years for more than 3,000 single-family homes

rebates.name: Clark Public Utilities residential rebates (Clark County, WA)
rebates.amount: Ductless heat pump $900 (replacing cable, baseboard, wall heaters or electric furnace); heat pump water heater (Tier 3 or 4) $1,500; smart thermostat $140 (instant via online marketplace); weatherization (windows, insulation) and income-qualified insulation rebates (amounts not shown on summary page)
rebates.whoQualifies: Clark Public Utilities customers; ductless heat pumps must be rated at least 7.5 HSPF2 and installed by a contractor licensed in Washington (self-installs don't qualify); weatherization rebates for electrically heated single-family and manufactured homes

rebates.name: Clark Public Utilities Heat Pump Program (Clark County, WA)
rebates.amount: Converting an electric forced-air furnace to a central heat pump $1,000, or to a central variable-speed heat pump $1,250; replacing a heat pump or electric zonal heat with a central variable-speed heat pump $500
rebates.whoQualifies: Clark Public Utilities customers in electrically heated homes; heat pumps must be rated at least 7.5 HSPF2 and installed by a contractor in the utility's Contractor Network; new construction qualifies unless it is in the New Homes Performance program
rebates.status: open; Clark Public Utilities says requirements and rebate amounts are 'subject to change without notice'

rebates.name: Washington State HEAR - City of Vancouver (WA) administrator
rebates.runBy: City of Vancouver, Washington, with Washington Commerce Climate Commitment Act funds
rebates.amount: City of Vancouver (WA) award $500,000; rebate amounts set by the local administrator (not published by Commerce)
rebates.whoQualifies: Households at or below 150% AMI (eligibility varies by administrator)
rebates.status: awarded; Commerce lists the City of Vancouver, Washington, among 40 local administrators (page updated September 8, 2026)

rebates.name: Cooling Portland (PCEF portable heat pump cooling units)
rebates.runBy: City of Portland PCEF (Earth Advantage as equipment purchasing partner)
rebates.amount: Free portable heat pump cooling/heating unit installed
rebates.whoQualifies: Low-income Portlanders at high risk of heat illness (priority to people over 60, with medical conditions, or living alone)
rebates.status: closed to new applications; previous applicants are on a waitlist

stateHomeEnergyRebates.status: not launched: ODOE says 'No rebates are available at this time'; contractor enrollment opens Monday, October 12, 2026; no date set for homeowner applications because U.S. DOE approval to launch is still required
stateHomeEnergyRebates.programName: Oregon Home Energy Rebate Programs: Home Efficiency Rebates (HOMES) and Home Electrification and Appliance Rebates (HEAR)
stateHomeEnergyRebates.administrator: Oregon Department of Energy; delivered by Energy Trust of Oregon (investor-owned utility areas) and Earth Advantage (consumer-owned utility areas)
stateHomeEnergyRebates.summary: ODOE was awarded over $113 million in September 2024. HOMES will pay performance-based rebates for whole-home efficiency at all income levels (50-100% of project cost up to $10,000, depending on savings and income). HEAR will pay 50-100% of costs up to $14,000 for households at or below 150% AMI for heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, electric cooking, dryers and related electrical work (heat pump water heaters, stoves and dryers must replace existing electric appliances). Washington-side Clark County residents fall under Washington's IRA programs, which also have not launched (Commerce says it is in the final stage of DOE authorization).

incomeQualified.name: Multnomah County Weatherization: Free Home Energy Upgrades
incomeQualified.runBy: Multnomah County Department of County Human Services (503-988-7423, weatherization.team@multco.us)
incomeQualified.summary: Free energy audit and cost-effective weatherization for eligible households; apply online (owners of apartment buildings apply for their buildings). The County warned of high pre-screen volume and up to 4 weeks for a response (page reviewed August 21, 2026).

incomeQualified.name: Oregon Weatherization Assistance Program (statewide)
incomeQualified.runBy: Oregon Housing and Community Services through local subgrantee agencies
incomeQualified.summary: Free weatherization for households at or below 200% of the federal poverty level; households may be placed on a waiting list; apply with your county's local agency.

incomeQualified.name: Clark County Weatherization Program (Washington side)
incomeQualified.runBy: Clark County (855-353-4328), listed by Washington Commerce
incomeQualified.summary: Free weatherization for Clark County households up to 200% FPL, 60% of state median income or 80% AMI.

incomeQualified.name: Energy Trust Savings Within Reach
incomeQualified.summary: Higher cash incentives for income-qualified homeowners (e.g., $3,000 instead of $1,000 for a ducted heat pump replacing an electric furnace; $1.50 vs $1.25/sq ft attic insulation).

incomeQualified.name: Energy Friendly Homes (PCEF)
incomeQualified.summary: No- or low-cost insulation, heat pump and heat pump water heater upgrades for Portland homeowners below 150% AMI.

incomeQualified.name: Income-Qualified Bill Discount (PGE and Pacific Power)
incomeQualified.summary: Monthly bill discount for households at or below State Median Income; Energy Trust says no financial documents are required to apply.

incomeQualified.name: Community Energy Project
incomeQualified.runBy: Community Energy Project (nonprofit, described on Energy Trust's community resources page)
incomeQualified.summary: In-home weatherization and safety repairs for low-income seniors and people with disabilities, plus free workshops.

localRules.name: Portland Home Energy Score ordinance
localRules.appliesTo: Ordinary homeowners: sellers who publicly advertise most single-family homes within Portland's jurisdictional boundary (townhome-style condos included; stacked units, mobile, manufactured and floating homes excepted); private sales never advertised are exempt
localRules.summary: Sellers must obtain a Home Energy Score and Report before listing and include it in all advertisements; reports stay valid up to eight years if no assessed changes were made; exemptions for financial distress or uninhabitable homes; assistance is offered for income-qualified sellers.

localRules.name: City of Milwaukie Home Energy Score requirement
localRules.appliesTo: Home sellers in Milwaukie (details on Milwaukie's website, not verified here)
localRules.summary: Portland's HES page says 'The City of Milwaukie also has Home Energy Score requirements'; Milwaukie's own rules were not reviewed.

localRules.name: Portland Commercial Building Energy Reporting
localRules.appliesTo: Commercial buildings 20,000 sq ft and larger; not homes
localRules.summary: Owners track and report energy performance by April 22 each year.

localRules.name: Oregon Building Performance Standard (HB 3409, 2023)
localRules.appliesTo: Commercial buildings (size thresholds not quoted on the page reviewed); not single-family homes
localRules.summary: Statewide energy performance standard for existing commercial buildings; compliance data now goes through ODOE's BEAM portal, and ODOE is taking applications for its Building Energy Reduction Incentive Program.

localRules.name: Washington Clean Buildings Performance Standard (Clark and Skamania counties)
localRules.appliesTo: Washington buildings over 20,000 sq ft, including multifamily over 20,000 sq ft; not single-family homes
localRules.summary: Tier 1 reporting deadlines June 1, 2026-June 1, 2028 by size; Tier 2 reporting due July 1, 2027.

localRules.name: Portland Multifamily Energy Reporting and Tenant Notice (proposal)
localRules.summary: BPS took public comment on a 2024 proposal to expand energy reporting and tenant notice in multifamily buildings and then ran a pilot; the project page does not show it as adopted.

notes: Portland's Home Energy Score requirement at listing remains in force and is the main rule that touches ordinary homeowners in this metro. Oregon's IRA rebates are still not available, but contractor enrollment opened on October 12, 2026 (the date of this check). Several state heat pump programs are exhausted for Portland homeowners: HP3's owner-occupied funds are fully reserved, the Community Heat Pump Deployment Program's Metro region is fully reserved, and the Rental Home Heat Pump Program's general funds are reserved. PCEF's Climate Investment Plan now funds 37 strategic programs, including city operations such as streetcar replacement, LED streetlighting and hydroelectric relicensing, alongside home programs like Energy Friendly Homes ($140 million) and Cooling Portland (closed to new applications). We found no in-home assessment offer on Energy Trust's residential pages; its assessment is online. Washington County, Clackamas County, Columbia County, Yamhill County and Skamania County weatherization agencies were not individually verified (OHCS's page does not list them in its static text); Washington Commerce lists CAC of Lewis, Mason and Thurston for Skamania. Federal home-efficiency tax credits are over: the IRS says 25C covered improvements made through December 31, 2025, and 25D is not available for property placed in service after December 31, 2025.
